endorsements.quote: Health professions programs should prepare learners to use GenAI responsibly, document competence in ways that account for AI use, support coaching for judgment and selfregulation, and clarify institutional standards for trustworthy learning, assessment, and credentialing.

unlisted_practices: Educators should design learning activities in which AI use is visible, discussable, and assessable.
Educators should model responsible use by showing how they verify AI-generated materials before using them in teaching, feedback, or assessment.

Course leaders and curriculum deans should move beyond isolated policies that simply permit or prohibit AI and specify where AI use is expected or inappropriate, how disclosure should occur, how learner judgment will be assessed, and how faculty will be supported.
Learners should use GenAI as a dialogue partner or study coach rather than as a simple chatbot or authority.
Learners should disclose when AI shaped their preparation, writing, or reasoning.
Health professions educators should coach learners in critical appraisal of AI-generated explanations, summaries, and recommendations, including source evaluation and corroboration.
Health professions programs should teach learners to recognize when AI-generated advice is insufficient and when human expertise must supersede it.

screen.reason: This is a perspective piece discussing the impact and institutional standards/guidance for generative AI in health professions education.
